summary: Primary documentation supports the implementation options, while controlled studies show that prompt order and formatting can materially change results. The studies justify exact version identity; they do not by themselves prove that a particular registry workflow improves team productivity.

items.text: LangSmith prompt commits, Git sync and structured run records
Langfuse prompt version control and trace linkage
Historical Humanloop implementation and official 2025 platform-sunset notice
Semantic Kernel version-controlled YAML prompt templates
OpenAI, Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock prompt versioning
Agent Studio prompt registry reference implementation, in progress

Lu et al. (ACL 2022) show that the order of few-shot examples can substantially affect model performance, providing direct evidence that seemingly small prompt-text changes require exact version attribution.

Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (ICLR 2024) evaluates formatting sensitivity across models and tasks, reinforcing the need to preserve the exact rendered prompt.

POSIX (Findings of EMNLP 2024) studies prompt sensitivity and robustness, adding evidence that prompt variants should be evaluated and linked to observed runs rather than treated as interchangeable prose.
